quizzes.topic: Arrhenius Concept and General Properties of Acids and Bases

questions.q: According to Arrhenius, an acid is a substance that in water produces:
questions.explanation: Arrhenius acids ionize in water to give H⁺ ions.

questions.q: According to Arrhenius, a base is a substance that in water produces:
questions.explanation: Arrhenius bases ionize in water to give OH⁻ ions.

questions.q: The Arrhenius theory was proposed in:
questions.explanation: Svante Arrhenius proposed it in 1887.

questions.q: Svante Arrhenius was a chemist from:
questions.explanation: He was a Swedish chemist.

questions.q: Acids have a ______ taste.
questions.explanation: Acids taste sour; bases taste bitter.

questions.q: Acids turn blue litmus paper:
questions.explanation: Acids change blue litmus to red.

questions.q: Which acid is used for removing scale from boilers?
questions.explanation: HCl is used for cleaning metals, bricks and removing scale from boilers.

questions.q: Phosphoric acid is used as:
questions.explanation: H₃PO₄ is used in fertilizers and as an acidulant for food.

questions.q: Which equation shows an Arrhenius base?
questions.explanation: KOH gives OH⁻ ions in water.

questions.q: A limitation of the Arrhenius theory is that it:
questions.explanation: It cannot explain substances like CO₂ and NH₃ outside water.

questions.q: Arrhenius theory cannot explain why NH₃ is a base because NH₃:
questions.explanation: There is no OH in NH₃, yet it is basic.

questions.q: Aqueous solutions of both acids and bases:
questions.explanation: Both produce ions in water, so they conduct electricity.

quizzes.topic: Bronsted–Lowry Concept of Acids and Bases

questions.q: According to Bronsted–Lowry, an acid is a:
questions.explanation: A Bronsted–Lowry acid donates a proton.

questions.q: According to Bronsted–Lowry, a base is a:
questions.explanation: A Bronsted–Lowry base accepts a proton.

questions.q: The Bronsted–Lowry theory was proposed in:
questions.explanation: Bronsted and Lowry proposed it independently in 1923.

questions.q: In HCl + H₂O → H₃O⁺ + Cl⁻, the base is:
questions.explanation: Water accepts the proton from HCl.

questions.q: In H₂O + NH₃ → NH₄⁺ + OH⁻, the acid is:
questions.explanation: Water donates a proton to NH₃.

questions.q: NH₃ is a Bronsted–Lowry base because it:
questions.explanation: NH₃ accepts H⁺ and forms NH₄⁺.

questions.q: Substances that react with both acids and bases are called:
questions.explanation: Water and Al₂O₃ are amphoteric.

questions.q: Water is amphoteric because it can:
options: both donate and accept a proton
questions.explanation: Water acts as acid with NH₃ and as base with HCl.

questions.q: After donating a proton, an acid generally forms a:
questions.explanation: e.g. HCl forms Cl⁻.

questions.q: After accepting a proton, a base generally forms a:
questions.explanation: e.g. NH₃ forms NH₄⁺.

questions.q: In H₂S + NH₃ → NH₄⁺ + HS⁻, H₂S acts as:
questions.explanation: H₂S donates a proton to NH₃.

questions.q: Which base of Bronsted–Lowry theory is also an Arrhenius base?
questions.explanation: All Bronsted bases except OH⁻ are not Arrhenius bases.

quizzes.topic: Strength of Acids and Bases, and Alkalis

questions.q: An acid that ionizes completely in aqueous solution is called:
questions.explanation: Strong acids ionize 100%.

questions.q: Which is a strong acid?
questions.explanation: HCl, HNO₃ and H₂SO₄ are strong acids.

questions.q: Ethanoic acid ionizes in water only up to about:
questions.explanation: So ethanoic acid is a weak acid.

questions.q: Which is a weak acid?
questions.explanation: Ethanoic acid ionizes partially.

questions.q: Which is a strong base?
questions.explanation: NaOH and KOH ionize completely.

questions.q: Ammonia is a weak base because it:
questions.explanation: It produces few OH⁻ ions.

questions.q: A base that is soluble in water is called:
questions.explanation: Alkalis are water-soluble bases.

questions.q: Which statement is correct?
questions.explanation: Only water-soluble bases are alkalis.

questions.q: Which base is NOT an alkali?
questions.explanation: Cu(OH)₂ is insoluble in water.

questions.q: Which household item contains an alkali?
questions.explanation: Soaps, detergents, shampoos and toothpaste contain alkali.

questions.q: Strong acids ionize in water:
questions.explanation: All molecules of strong acids ionize.

questions.q: Which is a weak base?
questions.explanation: Al(OH)₃ and NH₃ are weak bases.

quizzes.topic: Characteristic Properties of Acids and Acid Rain

questions.q: Metal + Acid →
questions.explanation: Acids react with metals to give salt and H₂.

questions.q: Zn + 2HCl →
questions.explanation: Zinc liberates hydrogen gas from HCl.

questions.q: Metal carbonate + Acid →
questions.explanation: Carbonates release CO₂ with acids.

questions.q: The gas liberated when acids react with carbonates is:
questions.explanation: CO₂ forms bubbles in water.

questions.q: Acid + Base → Salt + Water is called:
questions.explanation: Acids neutralize bases.

questions.q: HCl + NaOH →
questions.explanation: Neutralization gives salt and water.

questions.q: The reaction of carbonates with acids is used in the industrial preparation of:
questions.explanation: As stated for metal carbonate–acid reactions.

questions.q: Normal rain is slightly acidic due to dissolved:
questions.explanation: CO₂ dissolves in rainwater.

questions.q: Acid rain contains dissolved:
questions.explanation: Oxides of N and S form these acids.

questions.q: Acid rain damages statues made of marble because marble is a:
questions.explanation: Marble (CaCO₃) reacts with acids.

questions.q: Mg + H₂SO₄ →
questions.explanation: Magnesium gives hydrogen with sulphuric acid.

questions.q: Acids react with most metals and ______ them.
questions.explanation: Acids are corrosive.

quizzes.topic: Properties of Bases, Oxides and Hydroxides

questions.q: Bases have a ______ taste.
questions.explanation: Bases taste bitter.

questions.q: Bases turn red litmus paper:
questions.explanation: Bases change red litmus to blue.

questions.q: Aqueous solutions of bases feel:
questions.explanation: Bases have a slippery touch.

questions.q: On heating with ammonium salts, bases liberate:
questions.explanation: Base + ammonium salt → salt + NH₃ + water.

questions.q: NaOH + NH₄Cl →
questions.explanation: Ammonia is liberated.

questions.q: Bases are oxides or hydroxides of:
questions.explanation: Metal oxides/hydroxides are basic.

questions.q: 4Na + O₂ →
questions.explanation: Sodium forms sodium oxide.

questions.q: CaO + H₂O →
questions.explanation: Metal oxide + water → metal hydroxide.

questions.q: Oxide ions in water accept protons and become:
questions.explanation: O²⁻ + H₂O → 2OH⁻.

questions.q: Oxides that behave like both acids and bases are called:
questions.explanation: e.g. Al₂O₃ and ZnO.

questions.q: Which is an amphoteric oxide?
questions.explanation: ZnO reacts with both acids and bases.

questions.q: Magnesium burns in air to form:
questions.explanation: 2Mg + O₂ → 2MgO.

questions.q: Which of the following cannot be classified as an Arrhenius acid?
questions.explanation: CO₂ has no hydrogen to give H⁺ ions.

questions.q: Which of the following is a Bronsted base?
questions.explanation: NH₃ accepts a proton.

questions.q: Milk of magnesia contains Mg(OH)₂. It neutralizes excess stomach acid. Which salt is formed?
questions.explanation: Stomach acid is HCl: Mg(OH)₂ + 2HCl → MgCl₂ + 2H₂O.

questions.q: Ammonia is a base, because it:
options: ionizes in water to give OH⁻ ions
questions.explanation: In the Bronsted–Lowry sense NH₃ is a proton acceptor.

questions.q: In H₂O + HCl ⇌ H₃O⁺ + Cl⁻, which species is the proton acceptor?
questions.explanation: Water accepts the proton from HCl.
